newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker on Central Bank's cue.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker on Central Bank's cue.

text.p: * Slim turnover as traders cautious ahead of Fed meeting
The Philippine peso closed a tad weaker at 26.346 to the dollar from Wednesday's 26.343 as Central Bank started buying dollars by late afternoon, traders said.
"The Central Bank lifted the exchange rate in late afternoon, buying around $8 million at 26.345 and 26.347," one trader said. Traders were unsure about the Central Bank's motive.
Another trader said some banks were buying dollars to cover commercial demand.
The peso was generally steady, fluctuating between 26.341 and 26.348. The Central Bank posted its selling price at 26.348, keeping a floor on the depreciation.
Traders were cautious ahead of the U.S. Fed meeting next week. "We don't know if the U.S. will raise its rates or not," another trader said.
Foreign fund inflows were small despite the rally in the equities market in the morning. "We expect the inflows to come in in the coming days," he added.
